column6: Treasury OTA, Tax Expenditures FY2026 (27 Nov 2024), Table 1 line 5 'Deduction for foreign-derived intangible income derived from trade or business within the United States': $130,230M over FY2025-2034, divided by ten. Annual path FY2025-2034: 16420, 11200, 11540, 11880, 12240, 12610, 12990, 13380, 13780, 14190. PDF p. 25.
IRC section 250(a)(1)(A). Treasury OTA, Tax Expenditures FY2026, item 5 description, PDF p. 4.

IRC section 250(a)(3). The step-down is embedded in the published tax-expenditure path above (FY2025 $16.42B falls to FY2026 $11.20B), so the window average already reflects it; the module carries a single scalar and cannot express the year in which it happens.

fdii_deduction_tax_expenditure_billions / (fdii_deduction_rate * current_corporate_rate) = 13.023 / 0.07875. A window-average FDII-eligible income, not a tax-year-2025 level, because the tax expenditure it inverts spans the section 250(a)(3) step-down.
OECD Global Anti-Base Erosion Model Rules (Pillar Two). JCT, JCX-22-23, p. 3.

Substance-based income exclusion. JCT, JCX-22-23, p. 3: 'payroll and tangible assets, which are each excludable at a rate of five percent'. The payroll half is not modelled — Form 8975 reports employee counts, not payroll — which raises the modelled top-up by about 3% and leaves the overlap share unchanged.
IRC section 960(d): the GILTI foreign tax credit is limited to 80 percent of foreign taxes paid. JCT, JCX-22-23, p. 2.

Treasury OTA, Tax Expenditures FY2026, Table 1 line 4 'Reduced tax rate on active income of controlled foreign corporations (normal tax method)', PDF p. 25. The cost of the whole CFC active-income preference, which is what a GILTI rate rise to the statutory rate with QBAI eliminated would recover, less the section 245A exclusions it does not reach.

Treasury, General Explanations of the Administration's FY2025 Revenue Proposals, Table of Revenue Estimates, 'Revise the global minimum tax regime, limit inversions, and make related reforms', report p. 239 / PDF p. 247.

Same table, 'Adopt the undertaxed profits rule'. The module's UTPR returns $15B over the same window, one ninth of this, and that gap is the largest single residual in the biden_full_international row.

Same table, 'Repeal the deduction for foreign-derived intangible income'. Treasury pairs it one-for-one with 'Provide additional support for research and development expenditures' at -$157,993M and prints an explicit subtotal of $0. The gross row exceeds the tax expenditure above by 21% because Green Book proposals are scored on a baseline that already carries the same volume's 28% corporate rate: 130.230 * (28/21) = 173.6, less behaviour.

Same table, 'Subtotal; Reform International Taxation', report p. 240 / PDF p. 248. The carried benchmark for biden_full_international is -$700B; the three provisions the module implements sum to $510,232M of it.
JCT, JCX-22-23, Table 2, 'Rest of the world does not enact Pillar Two; United States enacts Pillar Two in 2025, but no U.S. UTPR', p. 10. This is the scenario create_pillar_two_adoption models.
JCT, JCX-22-23, Table 2, same but including a US UTPR, p. 10. Scenario 5 less Scenario 4 prices a US UTPR at $133.9B, within 2% of Treasury's own $136.313B row.

JCT, JCX-22-23, Table 2, 'Rest of the world enacts Pillar Two in 2025; United States also enacts Pillar Two in 2025', p. 10. In the state of the world where others have enacted, US adoption is a revenue *loss* — the opposite sign to the carried benchmark.
